subject: ss-cardiology
title: Pulmonary hypertension: classification, invasive hemodynamics and targeted pathway therapies

steps.tx: **Pulmonary hypertension** is defined invasively by right heart catheterization as a mean pulmonary arterial pressure > 20 mmHg at rest, lowered from the historical 25 mmHg threshold. Clinical classification stratifies patients into 5 clinical groups to guide distinct diagnostic and therapeutic pathways.
steps.say: Pulmonary hypertension is defined invasively by right heart catheterization as a resting mean pulmonary arterial pressure greater than twenty millimetres of mercury. The World Health Organization clinical classification stratifies patients into five distinct groups to direct specific diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

rows: PH due to left heart disease (HFpEF/HFrEF/valves)
Treat underlying left heart disease; vasodilators harm
PH due to lung diseases and hypoxia (COPD/ILD)
Oxygen and pulmonary optimization; vasodilators harm
PH with unclear or multifactorial mechanisms
Individualized therapy directed at primary disease

steps.tx: **Pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension** (including Group 1 PAH, Group 3 lung disease, and Group 4 CTEPH) requires mean PAP > 20 mmHg, pulmonary capillary wedge pressure <= 15 mmHg, and pulmonary vascular resistance > 2 Wood units on resting right heart catheterization, confirming isolated pulmonary vascular remodeling without left heart congestion.
steps.say: Pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension, encompassing pulmonary arterial hypertension and chronic thromboembolic disease, requires a resting mean pulmonary pressure over 20 millimetres of mercury, a pulmonary capillary wedge pressure up to 15, and pulmonary vascular resistance exceeding two Wood units. Detailed mastery of these diagnostic thresholds and hemodynamic criteria is essential for clinical examination excellence.

rows: Defines the presence of pulmonary hypertension
Excludes left ventricular elevated filling pressure

steps.tx: **Post-capillary pulmonary hypertension** due to left heart disease (Group 2) requires mean PAP > 20 mmHg and PCWP > 15 mmHg. It is subclassified into isolated post-capillary (IpcPH with PVR <= 2 Wood units) and combined post- and pre-capillary (CpcPH with PVR > 2 Wood units), reflecting secondary precapillary remodeling.
steps.say: Post-capillary pulmonary hypertension due to left heart disease requires mean pulmonary pressure over 20 millimetres of mercury with a wedge pressure exceeding 15. It is divided into isolated post-capillary with resistance up to two Wood units, and combined post- and pre-capillary when resistance exceeds two Wood units.

left.title: Isolated Post-Capillary (IpcPH)
points: PCWP > 15 mmHg, PVR <= 2 Wood units; passive retrograde transmission of elevated left atrial pressure alone.

right.title: Combined Post- and Pre-Capillary (CpcPH)
points: PCWP > 15 mmHg, PVR > 2 Wood units; chronic retrograde venous hypertension triggers reactive arteriolar remodeling.

steps.tx: **Endothelin receptor antagonists** (bosentan, ambrisentan, macitentan) block endothelin-1-mediated vasoconstriction, cellular proliferation, and vascular remodeling in pulmonary arterial hypertension. Ambrisentan selectively blocks ETA receptors, while bosentan and macitentan provide dual ETA and ETB receptor antagonism. Clinical mastery requires rigorous recognition of these diagnostic thresholds and hemodynamic criteria.
steps.say: Endothelin receptor antagonists, including ambrisentan, bosentan, and macitentan, block endothelin-1-mediated vasoconstriction and vascular remodeling in pulmonary arterial hypertension. Ambrisentan selectively blocks ETA receptors, while bosentan and macitentan antagonize both ETA and ETB receptors. Detailed mastery of these diagnostic thresholds and hemodynamic criteria is essential for clinical examination excellence.

rows: Peripheral edema, nasal congestion; low hepatotoxicity
Dual ETA/ETB with high tissue penetration
Anemia, headache; no monthly liver monitoring required

steps.tx: **Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors** (sildenafil, tadalafil) and soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators (riociguat) enhance nitric oxide-cGMP vasodilation in PAH. Co-administration of PDE-5 inhibitors and riociguat is strictly contraindicated due to synergistic cGMP accumulation causing profound refractory systemic hypotension and syncope. Clinical mastery requires rigorous recognition of these diagnostic thresholds and hemodynamic criteria.
steps.say: Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors such as sildenafil and tadalafil, along with the soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator riociguat, enhance nitric oxide-mediated cyclic GMP vasodilation in pulmonary arterial hypertension. Co-administration of PDE-5 inhibitors with riociguat is strictly contraindicated due to lethal hypotension. Detailed mastery of these diagnostic thresholds and hemodynamic criteria is essential for clinical examination excellence.

left.title: PDE-5 Inhibitors
points: Sildenafil and tadalafil prevent cyclic GMP degradation by vascular smooth muscle phosphodiesterase type 5.

right.title: Strict Contraindication
points: Concomitant use of riociguat with PDE-5 inhibitors is contraindicated due to catastrophic systemic hypotension.

steps.tx: Prostacyclin pathway agonists, including continuous intravenous **epoprostenol**, treprostinil, and the oral IP receptor agonist **selexipag**, induce direct pulmonary vasodilation and platelet anti-aggregation. Continuous intravenous epoprostenol remains the gold standard Class I therapy proven to improve survival in high-risk NYHA functional class IV PAH.
steps.say: Prostacyclin pathway agonists, including intravenous epoprostenol and the oral selective IP receptor agonist selexipag, induce potent pulmonary vasodilation and inhibit platelet aggregation. Continuous intravenous epoprostenol remains the only medical therapy proven to improve survival in high-risk class IV PAH. Detailed mastery of these diagnostic thresholds and hemodynamic criteria is essential for clinical examination excellence.

steps.tx: **Sotatercept** represents a first-in-class activin signaling inhibitor engineered as an activin receptor type IIA-Fc fusion protein. In the STELLAR trial, sotatercept restored biological balance between pro-proliferative activin and growth differentiation factors and antiproliferative BMPR2 signaling, substantially reducing pulmonary vascular resistance and improving exercise capacity.
steps.say: Sotatercept is a first-in-class activin signaling inhibitor engineered as an activin receptor type IIA-Fc fusion protein. Evaluated in the STELLAR trial, sotatercept rebalances pro-proliferative activin and antiproliferative BMPR2 signaling, significantly reducing pulmonary vascular resistance in PAH. Detailed mastery of these diagnostic thresholds and hemodynamic criteria is essential for clinical examination excellence.

left.title: Sotatercept Mechanism
points: Traps activin A and growth factors; reverses pulmonary arteriolar hyperproliferation and vascular wall thickening.

right.title: STELLAR Trial Benefit
points: Significant 6-minute walk distance increase, marked PVR reduction, and 84% reduction in death or clinical worsening.

steps.tx: **Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension** (CTEPH, Group 4) is diagnosed by ventilation-perfusion (V/Q) scintigraphy demonstrating mismatched segmental perfusion defects. Surgical **pulmonary endarterectomy** (PEA) under deep hypothermic circulatory arrest represents the potentially curative treatment of choice for surgically accessible proximal thromboembolic disease.
steps.say: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension is diagnosed with ventilation-perfusion scanning demonstrating mismatched segmental perfusion defects. Surgical pulmonary endarterectomy under deep hypothermic circulatory arrest represents the potentially curative treatment of choice for accessible thromboembolic disease. Detailed mastery of these diagnostic thresholds and hemodynamic criteria is essential for clinical examination excellence.

steps.tx: This ventilation perfusion scan shows normal even ventilation on the left with multiple wedge shaped segmental perfusion gaps on the right in apical and basal zones. This **mismatch pattern** points to organised clot blocking flow rather than airway disease. In suspected Group 4 disease this scan is the diagnostic gate, because confirmed **chronic thromboembolism** with accessible lesions makes **pulmonary endarterectomy** the potentially curative option.
steps.say: On the left the lungs ventilate evenly, so air reaches all zones. On the right several wedge shaped segments receive no blood flow, including apical and basal areas. Air without blood in a segmental pattern means vessels are blocked, the classic picture of chronic thromboembolic disease. That mismatch is what makes this scan the key test, since suitable patients can be offered curative surgery to clear the organised clot.

vis.alt: Ventilation perfusion scan shows normal ventilation with multiple mismatched wedge shaped segmental perfusion defects.
